pure-announcement.rationale: It is an academic survey proposing and defending a taxonomy from cited prior systems, not a launch, release or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: The nearest existing concepts (react-pattern, evolved-llm-coordinator, workflows-versus-agents, rl-learned-orchestration, multi-agent-orchestration-topologies, outcome-based-agent-evals) each cover one specific pattern or mechanism; none give the overall six-part decomposition (Perception, Brain, Planning, Action, Tool Use, Collaboration) this note proposes as a shared vocabulary for comparing systems.

unfalsifiable.rationale: It is a cited academic survey (with a bibliography of prior systems and papers) rather than an assertion, and is exactly the kind of evidence-grounded alternative this hunt was sent to find in place of an unsupported consultancy framing.

durability.rationale: Unlike the original consultancy piece, this taxonomy is derived from a systematic review of published agent architectures rather than an asserted market observation, and a categorisation scheme for what an agent system must do (perceive, reason, plan, act, use tools, collaborate) does not depend on any vendor's product cycle.

actionability.rationale: It gives a structural checklist for designing or evaluating an agent platform — treat perception, reasoning, planning, action, tool use and collaboration as separable concerns to be deliberately designed, rather than an undifferentiated agent loop — which changes how someone would decompose a build.

atomicity.rationale: The source is a 99KB survey bundling the taxonomy together with several other separable ideas (the shift to native inference-time reasoning models, MCP/tool-use standardisation, evaluation practice, specific failure modes like prompt injection); the taxonomy itself is one coherent paragraph-statable idea, but the note as a whole is not.

proposed_concepts.title: Six-part agentic AI architecture taxonomy
proposed_concepts.definition: A unified taxonomy for describing an agentic AI system by decomposing it into six architectural concerns — Perception (taking in state from the environment), Brain (the LLM-based reasoning core), Planning (decomposing a goal into a sequence of actions), Action (executing a step and observing its effect), Tool Use (invoking external capabilities, increasingly through standardised protocols rather than one-off API integrations), and Collaboration (coordinating with other agents or humans) — giving a common vocabulary for comparing systems ranging from a single reasoning loop to hierarchical multi-agent deployments.
